title: Fees and charges (overnight funding, 1:1 exemption, instrument table)
summary: Funding = benchmark (SOFR) ± 4%/yr fee; 1:1 positions on 'most markets' pay no overnight funding except Natural Gas, US Cocoa, VIX and TRY pairs.

title: Capital.com introduces 0% overnight funding to support investment-style trading; overnight fee adjustment page
summary: 8 Jul 2024: no overnight funding on 1:1 CFD trades in shares and crypto; 89% of non-leveraged overnight positions were stocks and crypto.

title: Help Centre: Dividends (calculation, timing, markets, adjustments)
summary: Share and index CFDs: long credited size × dividend (adjusted for tax if necessary), short debited, on the ex-dividend date.

title: Projected Dividends for 12-18.10.2026 (index dividend points)
summary: Weekly table of projected index dividend adjustments in points per day (US500, US100, US30 posted 21:00 UK); longs receive, shorts pay.

title: Overnight funding calculation; how dividend payments affect CFD positions
summary: IG charges 3% ± benchmark ÷ 360/365 at 22:00 UK, three days on Friday; dividend adjustments on the ex-date for positions held into the open.

title: CFD overnight fees
summary: Non-leveraged stock buys are real shares with no overnight fee; leveraged stock longs pay 6.4% + benchmark; weekend triple charge on Friday or Wednesday by asset.

title: FAQ: dividends, corporate events, overnight funding
summary: Equity/ETF CFD positions open on the ex-date get a dividend adjustment (positive for buys, negative for sells); funding rate per instrument under Details.

title: Marginal stockholder tax rates and the clientele effect
authors: Edwin J. Elton, Martin J. Gruber
summary: NYSE 1966-67: prices drop by less than the dividend on ex-days (ratio about 0.78), most for low-yield stocks, interpreted as a tax clientele effect.

title: Marginal stockholder tax effects and ex-dividend-day price behavior: evidence from taxable versus non-taxable closed-end funds
authors: Edwin J. Elton, Martin J. Gruber, Christopher R. Blake
summary: Natural experiment with closed-end funds shows ex-day price behaviour follows tax treatment and changes with tax law, supporting the tax explanation.

title: Taxes, order imbalance and abnormal returns around the ex-dividend day
authors: Andrew Ainsworth, Kingsley Fong, David Gallagher, Graham Partington
summary: Australian data: dividend-seeking buying pressure lifts prices before the ex-day and reverses afterwards; rejects the bid-ask bounce explanation.

title: The dividend month premium
authors: Samuel M. Hartzmark, David H. Solomon
summary: US 1927-2009: stocks in predicted dividend months earn 0.24-0.53% a month abnormal (value/equal weighted), rising into the ex-day and negative after.

title: The earnings announcement premium and trading volume
summary: Stocks earn 61 bp a month more in expected announcement months (about 7% a year, from 1927), including a 25 bp run-up in the 10 days before.

title: The earnings announcement premium around the globe
authors: Brad M. Barber, Emmanuel De George, Reuven Lehavy, Brett Trueman
summary: Announcement-month premium of over 11% a year across 46 countries, larger for the smallest stocks, linked to investor attention.

title: The disappearing earnings announcement premium
authors: Amanda Rae Heitz, Gans Narayanamoorthy, Morad Zekhnini
summary: The US earnings announcement premium disappeared after the 2004 8-K disclosure rule (weekly premium 23.9 bp lower), while it survives abroad.

title: Rest in peace post-earnings announcement drift
summary: Prices now fully reflect earnings surprises on the announcement day; PEAD has been non-existent for large stocks since 2006.

title: Limited attention and the earnings announcement returns of past stock market winners
authors: David Aboody, Reuven Lehavy, Brett Trueman
summary: 1971-2005: top past-12-month winners earn +1.58% in the 5 days before earnings and -1.86% in the 5 days after, attributed to retail attention.

title: The disappearing index effect
summary: S&P 500 addition abnormal return fell from 3.4% (1980s) and 7.6% (1990s) to 0.8% in 2010-2020; Tesla 2020 was the outlier.

title: Nasdaq-100 special rebalance (July 2023) and NDX methodology
summary: Special rebalance when names above 4.5% exceed 48% of NDX (cut to 40%), done 24 Jul 2023; quarterly reweights after the third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec.

title: A tug of war: overnight versus intraday expected returns
authors: Dong Lou, Christopher Polk, Spyros Skouras
summary: Momentum profits are earned overnight and reversal intraday; firm-level overnight and intraday returns each persist for years.

title: Does overnight news explain overnight returns?
authors: Paul Glasserman, Kriste Krstovski, Paul Laliberte, Harry Mamaysky
summary: Nearly all US stock gains over 30 years came overnight; news topics from 2.4 million articles explain much of the overnight/intraday gap.

title: Market return around the clock: a puzzle
summary: E-mini S&P: the whole average return comes in the 4 hours around the European open (23:30-03:30 ET), 7.6% a year with Sharpe 1.67.

title: Strikingly suspicious overnight and intraday returns
summary: Argues the positive-overnight, negative-intraday pattern of major indices is too regular to be benign; contested.

title: The role of shorting, firm size, and time on market anomalies
summary: Momentum profits show no reliable relation with firm size (unlike value), so momentum exists among the largest stocks.

title: Market concentration and the Magnificent Seven (Russell, Goldman via Quartz, Columbia Threadneedle, Schroders)
summary: Top-10 share of the S&P 500 near 39% (2025) vs 27% in 2000; Mag 7 made over 62% of 2023's gain; no academic test that concentration predicts returns.

title: Do stocks outperform Treasury bills?
summary: Most US stocks underperform T-bills over their lives; 4% of stocks created all net wealth 1926-2016, so dominance by a few is normal.

title: Are there seasonal intraday or overnight anomalies in Bitcoin? / The seasonality of Bitcoin
summary: Buying BTC at 21:00 UTC and selling at 23:00 UTC earned 33-41% a year before costs (2015-2023), with a rough 2022-23.

title: Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects in returns and trading volume
authors: Dirk G. Baur, Daniel Cahill, Keith Godfrey, Zhangxin Liu
summary: Over 15 million observations from seven exchanges: time-varying calendar effects but no consistent or persistent return patterns.

title: Periodicity in cryptocurrency volatility and liquidity
authors: Peter Reinhard Hansen, Chan Kim, Wade Kimbrough
summary: BTC/ETH volatility and volume have strong day-of-week (low weekends) and hour-of-day patterns, growing stronger and tied to perp funding times.

title: Risks and returns of cryptocurrency
summary: 2011-2018: strong time-series momentum in crypto at daily and 1-4 week horizons and attention-based predictability; no exposure to stock factors.

title: Estimating the impact of the Bitcoin halving on its price using synthetic control
summary: Synthetic control finds a positive 2024 halving effect after 3 months (about a fifth of the price rise) but no robust effect for 2020.

title: Volatility harvesting: extracting return from randomness
summary: Rebalancing between volatile assets (or asset and cash) creates growth that scales with variance and vanishes at correlation 1; tested on real data.

title: Shannon's Demon and how returns can be created out of thin air (HN thread)
summary: Debate on rebalancing 50/50 with cash: it converts arithmetic return into geometric growth; not free money, loses to strong trends.

title: Fundamentals of perpetual futures
authors: Songrun He, Asaf Manela, Omri Ross, Victor von Wachter
summary: No-arbitrage pricing of perpetuals; funding rates make longs pay shorts; crypto deviations are large, co-move and shrink over time.

title: Perp funding rates as a bottom signal (K33 Research via The Block)
summary: After BTC 30-day average funding turned negative (7 episodes since 2018) the 90-day return averaged +79%; tiny sample, unverified.

title: Volatility-managed portfolios
summary: Scaling exposure by inverse recent variance raises Sharpe ratios of the market and factor portfolios in-sample.

title: On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios
authors: Scott Cederburg, Michael S. O'Doherty, Feifei Wang, Xuemin (Sterling) Yan
summary: Across 103 strategies, real-time volatility-managed versions do not systematically beat the unmanaged originals out of sample.

title: Own check on the lab candles: hour of day, weekends, overnight vs intraday, rebalancing, rollover, basket tracking
summary: Descriptive stats on Capital.com 1-minute candles 2024-01 to 2026-09 with the scripts in files/unlevered/own-check/.
